verses.text: Abijah died and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa became king after him. While Asa was king, the land had peace for ten years.
Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He removed the altars to foreign gods and the hilltop shrines. He smashed the stone pillars and cut down the Asherah poles.
He told the people of Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and to obey his law and commands.
He also removed the hilltop shrines and the incense altars from all the towns of Judah. The kingdom had peace while he ruled.
He built walled towns in Judah, because the land was at peace. There was no war in those years, because the LORD gave him rest.

He said to the people of Judah, "Let's build up these towns and put walls around them, with towers, gates, and bars. The land is still ours, because we have looked to the LORD our God. We looked to him, and he has given us peace on every side." So they built and did well.

Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and two hundred eighty thousand men from Benjamin, armed with small shields and bows. All of them were brave, strong soldiers.
Zerah from Ethiopia came out to fight them with an army of a million soldiers and three hundred chariots. He came as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him, and they lined up for battle in the Zephathah Valley near Mareshah.

Asa cried out to the LORD his God, "LORD, no one but you can help the weak against the strong. Help us, LORD our God, because we trust in you. In your name we have come against this huge army. LORD, you are our God. Do not let any man win against you."
So the LORD defeated the Ethiopians in front of Asa and Judah, and the Ethiopians ran away.
Asa and his army chased them as far as Gerar. So many Ethiopians fell that they could not recover. They were crushed by the LORD and his army. The men of Judah carried off a huge amount of loot.
They destroyed all the towns around Gerar, because the fear of the LORD had fallen on them. They took everything of value from those towns, because there was a lot to take.
They also attacked the camps of the herders and took many sheep and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
